amalfi.overview: The steep cliffs and terraced hillsides above the Mediterranean offer excellent day hikes, led by the famous Path of the Gods. This moderate route follows the high ridges between Bomerano and Nocelle, delivering sweeping views of the coastline and the sea. Other trails explore deep gorges like the Valle delle Ferriere, passing waterfalls and ruins. Most trailheads are reached by local bus or by hiking up from the coastal towns.

badlands-black-hills.overview: The region offers two distinct landscapes for day hikers: the exposed, eroded pinnacles of the Badlands and the shaded ponderosa pine forests of the Black Hills. Trails range from easy prairie loops to the strenuous climb up Black Elk Peak, which rewards hikers with views of granite spires. The 111-mile Centennial Trail provides a multi-day trek through the hills and plains. Spring and autumn offer the most reliable weather across both areas.

barcelona.overview: The best hiking lies just outside the city, with the serrated peaks of Montserrat offering strenuous day hikes to the Sant Jeroni summit for views stretching to the Pyrenees. Closer in, the wooded ridges of the Collserola range provide moderate trails above the city, easily reached by funicular or train. The Mediterranean climate makes hiking possible year-round, though summer afternoons are intensely hot.

bavaria-munich.overview: The real hiking is about an hour and a half south of the city in the Bavarian Alps, where trains and cable cars lift hikers to high ridge trails above alpine lakes. The network around Garmisch and Mittenwald offers everything from easy valley loops to strenuous limestone summits and multi-day hut-to-hut routes.

beijing.overview: The hiking here is defined by the Great Wall, offering routes along ancient stone paths and crumbling watchtowers that trace the mountain ridges. Visitors typically take a shuttle or cable car to reach restored sections like Mutianyu and Jinshanling for moderate day hikes, while wild stretches like Jiankou offer strenuous scrambling. The best hiking is in spring and autumn when the air is clear and temperatures are mild.

belfast-giants-causeway.overview: The coastal cliffs and heather-covered granite peaks offer strong regional hiking, anchored by the Causeway Coast Way, a 33-mile trek over two to three days past basalt columns and ruined castles. Day hikers head to the Mourne Mountains for strenuous, steep climbs up Slieve Donard, or the Glens of Antrim for moderate forest and waterfall loops. The trails are best from May to September, though rain is possible year-round.

bhutan.overview: Bhutan offers some of the most dramatic and remote hiking in the Himalayas, from steep forest day hikes to legendary high-altitude expedition treks. The steep climb to the cliffside Tiger's Nest monastery is the headline day hike, while the multi-week Snowman Trek and the shorter Druk Path Trek cross remote passes beneath unclimbed peaks. All hiking requires a licensed guide and a daily fee, keeping the trails pristine. The best hiking is in spring and autumn.

black-forest.overview: The Black Forest offers a vast network of trails through dense conifers, open pastures, and deep gorges, with cable cars lifting hikers to the higher ridges. The Westweg is a famous 177-mile trek running the length of the region in about two weeks. Day hikes range from easy lakeside paths to moderate climbs up the Feldberg, the highest peak.

borabora.overview: French Polynesia offers rugged, steep jungle trails leading to volcanic viewpoints, though the network is modest. On Bora Bora, the strenuous scramble up Mount Pahia requires a guide, while the shoulder of Mount Otemanu offers a challenging day hike beneath the sheer summit cliffs. The best hiking is found from May to October when the paths are drier and less slippery.
